section_summary: This section contains State Department and SCAP records concerning Japanese educational reform, beginning with translations of Japanese educational periodicals and an unrelated misfiled consular telegram exchange regarding a Philippine trainee in Rio de Janeiro. It highlights internal discussions and Allied Council for Japan proceedings clarifying that remarks advocating centralized control over teachers and textbooks were made by the British member rather than American chairman William J. Sebald, alongside Soviet press critiques of SCAP educational policies. The remainder details administrative division of scientific and educational responsibilities within GHQ and transmits Parts of SCAP's comprehensive statistical survey and roster of Japanese educational institutions, focusing on Akita Prefecture.

subfiles.summary: Reviews articles on art and physical education by Chozo Saito, Kiyoshi Shingyoji, and Yoshihiko Kurimoto, concluding that progressive enthusiasm stirs Japanese education.
subfiles.title: Report on Japanese Educational Articles in Current Periodicals

subfiles.title: Newspaper Clipping: "New Exchange Rate Is Urged for Japan"

subfiles.about: Memorandum confirming from official Allied Council minutes that remarks opposing educational decentralization were made by the British member.

subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from John M. Allison to Frank A. Schuler, Jr. Concerning Allied Council Minutes

subfiles.about: Interoffice memo transmitting an advance copy of William J. Sebald's prepared address to refute the New York Times report.
subfiles.summary: Green transmits Sebald's prepared address, providing preliminary evidence that the New York Times report on educational decentralization was erroneous.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from Marshall Green to John M. Allison on Sebald's Remarks

subfiles.about: Official address delivered at the Allied Council for Japan outlining the progress and problems of Japanese educational reform.
subfiles.summary: Sebald details the comprehensive transformation of Japanese education under the Occupation. He reviews the purging of militaristic elements, decentralization of administrative control to prefectures, curricular revisions, teacher retraining, the new 6-3-3-4 ladder, and severe economic challenges including paper and teacher shortages.
subfiles.title: Statement by William J. Sebald at the Allied Council for Japan on Educational Reform

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch transmitting translated summaries of Soviet press articles criticizing American educational administration in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Moscow Embassy transmits translated press summaries by S. Maev criticizing Occupation educational policies, alleging reactionary persistence, religious influence, and reporting student conditions at Tokyo University.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1919 from Embassy Moscow: Transmitting Translated Summary of Articles on Japanese Education

subfiles.about: Translations of Soviet press excerpts criticizing Western capitalist education and American educational democratization in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Translated articles criticize American educational influence, alleging that SCAP preserves reactionary educational foundations, encourages Boy Scouts, supports religious missions, and suppresses leftist teachers' unions.
subfiles.title: Enclosure 1 to Despatch No. 1919: Translated Summaries of Articles from Teachers' Gazette

subfiles.about: Translation of S. Maev's article describing conditions, facilities, and political sentiment at Tokyo University.
subfiles.summary: Translated account describing neglected conditions, hidden prewar Russian books, impoverished faculty, and student Communist and Soviet-study circles at Tokyo Imperial University.
subfiles.title: Enclosure 2 to Despatch No. 1919: Translated Summary of "A Visit to Tokyo University" from Public Education

subfiles.about: Letter requesting SCAP's comments regarding Professor Robert King Hall's complaint of abridged religious freedom during SCAP textbook review.
subfiles.summary: Wisner transmits Professor Hall's letter alleging SCAP abridged religious freedom when reviewing the textbook "History of the West."
subfiles.title: Letter from Frank G. Wisner to Daniel Noce Regarding Robert King Hall Inquiry

subfiles.summary: This report compiles data on educational institutions in Akita Prefecture across national, prefectural, municipal, town/village, and private jurisdictions as of April and November 1946. It outlines administrative classifications, the pre-reform educational ladder, and data collection methodology. Extensive tables and directory listings provide dates of founding, student enrollments, and teacher counts for higher, vocational, middle, and girls' high schools.
subfiles.title: Roster and Statistics of Japanese Educational Institutions, Part 2: Akita Prefecture
